sam: FYI enabled FP8 kernels on L40s for the redwood-medium-13b canary and seeing a subtle but consistent regression on codegen tests. tiny syntax drops (missing punctuation) across many prompts, H100 FP8 looks fine though. anyone seen this?

maria: ping @kai — kernel/quant expert. can you grab diffs + logs?

sam: quick summary: baseline (fp16 @ H100) -> pass. fp8 on H100 -> pass. fp8 on L40s -> consistent ~1.7% drop exact-match on our code unit tests. example bad output: `def add(a, b) return a + b` (missing colon). Repro command i ran:
```bash
./tools/run_eval.sh --model redwood-medium-13b --precision fp8 --device l40s --prompts eval_code_snippets.json --seed 42
```

kai: that pattern smells like activation scaling/rounding differences. L40s fp8 kernels default to symmetric per-tensor scaling in our current kernel vs H100's per-channel scale. When LN inputs hit different ranges, rounding can push punctuation/paren tokens over the threshold. try switching quantizer to per_channel or enable compat_mode in the compiler. also check bias-folding during compilation.

sam: trying per_channel now. current runtime config: 
```json
{"precision":"fp8","quantizer":"per_channel","act_clip":"8.0","compat_mode":"false"}
```

ryan: also bisect by disabling prefix/KV caching + force batch_size=1 and seq_len=512. batching + tiling differences often amplify tiny fp8 rounding deltas into deterministic token shifts.

sam: ran per_channel + batch_size=1: exact-match recovered to within 0.1%. so looks like an interaction of per-tensor scaling + batching/tiling on L40s. i'll run a longer canary matrix (batch sizes 1,4,8 and seq 128/512).

infra-bot: Canary deployment started: fp8-l40s-perchannel (canary id: 2179993331) on pool l40s-canary-3 — image sha abc123 — started at 2026-03-20T12:02:10Z :rocket:

maria: great catch. if per_channel consistently fixes it, let's add a compatibility shim in the runtime that forces per_channel for L40s for models where layernorm occurs post-attention. open a PR and add a unit test that runs the small codegen eval.

kai: +1. also add a telemetry gauge for pre-LN activation max/min and a regression alert when distribution shifts > 2 sigma after an enablement. that'll help catch models that rely on very tight activation ranges.

sam: filing PR now — draft at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 (DRAFT). Plan: (1) enable per_channel by default for L40s in compat shim; (2) add telemetry counter for ln_pre_clip_max; (3) add canary matrix job with batch/seq permutations. will report back after 8-hour canary. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
